blocks.content: PFRDA acts as the principal regulatory body to promote old age income security by establishing, developing, and regulating pension funds.

items: PFRDA was established as a statutory regulatory body under the PFRDA Act, 2013.
Powers of search and seizure under the PFRDA Act require mandatory authorization from a Judicial Magistrate of the First Class.
PFRDA has the authority to adjudicate disputes between intermediaries and subscribers or between multiple intermediaries.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: PFRDA regulates the National Pension System (NPS) and other pension schemes not covered under any other central act.
Holds statutory powers to register, regulate, and oversee intermediaries like Central Recordkeeping Agencies (CRAs), Pension Funds, and Points of Presence (PoPs).
Empowered to conduct inquiries, call for information, inspect books of accounts, and perform audits of intermediaries.
Protects subscriber interests through standardizing operational rules and establishing robust grievance redressal mechanisms.
Possesses quasi-judicial powers to impose monetary penalties and initiate search and seizure procedures upon authorization.
